title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 历史古迹 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：prince　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 prince 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the clerk ① served the prince that no applicant in the office would have described, and he said the serving was the whole of the month. The ② prince, meaning the royal itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed undescribed in the book; a prince, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ prince in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ prince at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A prince, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the clerk said the describing is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the prince was the whole of the matter, meaning the hope and not the royal. The ⑥ prince, meaning the hope and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; prince, he said, is either something you serve or the only word that means both a royal and a hope. He said the hope is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ prince had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ prince of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of describing; prince, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ prince I remember is the royal described in the file, which closed in 1968 and is still described as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ prince, my mother said in 1970, is the only royal that improves by being described; every prince, she said, is a hope that has agreed to look like a royal. She said the hope was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 王子；亲王（指办事处里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 王子；亲王（指那位王子本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：serve the prince 侍奉这一位王子
D. n. 王子；亲王（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 王子之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的王子之事）
F. n. 王子；亲王（指卷宗里写到、被描述的那一位）
G. n. 王子、指望（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 指望（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: served the prince that no applicant in the office would have described
The prince, meaning the royal itself and not the stamp
the prince at the far counter
the prince was the whole of the matter
the prince had become a line in a file
The prince of the whole thing
A prince, my mother said in 1970

answers.why: serve the prince 意为“侍奉这一位王子”，1961 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯描述的一位王子做了一遍。
prince 意为“王子；亲王”，指那位王子本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。
prince 意为“王子；亲王”，指办事处里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
prince 意为“王子；亲王”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
prince 意为“王子、指望”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位指望就是那件事的全部。
prince 意为“指望”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位王子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
prince 意为“王子；亲王”，指卷宗里写到、被描述的那一位，到 1966 年这一位成了卷宗里的一行。
prince 意为“王子之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的王子之事是一处办事处和三个月份的描述。
prince 意为“王子；亲王”，我记得的是卷宗里描述过的那一位，1968 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一位。
prince 为抽象总称，母亲 1970 年说，王子是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的王子。
